questions.question: Q: State Kepler's three laws of planetary motion.

points.text: 1st: Planets orbit in ellipses with the Sun at one focus. 2nd: A line from planet to Sun sweeps equal areas in equal times. 3rd: T² is proportional to a³.

questions.question: Q: Why do planets move faster at perihelion?

points.text: Because of Kepler's second law — equal areas are swept in equal times, so the planet must move faster when closer to the Sun to cover the same area.

questions.question: Q: State Newton's law of gravitation and explain each term.

points.text: F = GMm/r². F is the gravitational force, G is the gravitational constant, M and m are the two masses, and r is the distance between their centres.

questions.question: Q: What is a geostationary orbit and what is it used for?

points.text: An orbit above the equator at ~36,000 km altitude with a 24-hour period, so the satellite appears stationary above a fixed point on Earth. Used for communications and weather satellites.

questions.question: Q: Calculate: if a planet orbits at 4 AU, what is its orbital period? (Use Kepler's 3rd law with Earth as reference.)

points.text: T² = a³, so T² = 4³ = 64, T = 8 years.
